core.title: Take spacing, radii, and durations from foundations tokens in UI files
core.given: The repository has a design root (the design-system tree; where it lives and how its layers are named comes from the profile) and you edit a UI file — any file that carries style declarations — anywhere outside its token-definition (foundations) layer
core.when: the file's style declarations set margin, padding, gap, inset, top/right/bottom/left, border-radius, or transition/animation — in any notation the stack's UI files use for style declarations (stylesheet syntax, style objects, inline or embedded styles in markup, markup authored inside source literals; per profile)
core.then: Take those lengths greater than 1px and non-zero durations from the design system's foundations tokens, referenced the way this stack references token values (per profile); never hardcode them.
prefer: Use the existing foundations scale for spacing, inset, radius, and duration.
During GREEN: reuse the nearest existing semantic or scale token.
During GREEN: add a foundation value only when the design genuinely needs a distinct one.
During GREEN: change only the style declaration the acceptance needs.
avoid: One-off tokens that merely rename a hardcoded literal.
unless: Value is 0 or 1px (hairlines are not design decisions).
A token definition itself (a declaration that defines a new token value), wherever it lives.
The file is in the design root's token-definition (foundations) layer.
A test file of any kind (unit, acceptance, or end-to-end), or a vendored/build (never-scanned) tree.
No design root in the repository: no system to connect to yet.
core.why: Spacing and motion are an interface's rhythm; each hardcoded length is a new step on a scale nobody chose, eroding it one component at a time.
evidence: The stack's design-token check reports no hardcoded spacing/inset/radius length > 1px or non-zero duration in affected UI files.
Prove: the current visual or behavioral acceptance passes, and affected UI values come from the declared foundations (token references to values defined once in foundations).
verification: Properties judged: margin, padding, gap, inset, top, right, bottom, left, border-radius (lengths > 1px); transition, animation (non-zero durations). Judged over the UI file's declarations — all declarations, not only changed ones.

Judged in every notation the stack's UI files use for style declarations (per profile): where such a notation treats a bare number as a length, it is judged as a length under the same > 1px threshold; markup authored inside host-language string or template literals is judged as markup (inline style attributes and style-block text); only authored literal text is judged — code, comments, regex literals, and interpolated spans are never read as declarations (a value spanning an interpolation is judged on its literal chunks alone).

Self-scoping: only repositories that have a design root (per profile) are judged; a repository with no design root is not judged — there is no system to connect to yet. The design root's token-definition layer defines these values and is itself not scanned.

A UI file is any file that carries style declarations, in any format, anywhere in the repository; there is no exhaustive format allowlist. A realization's detector may currently cover only some file kinds — that is implementation coverage, not a limit on applicability.

Exclusions: test files of every kind — the union of the profile's unit-test, acceptance-test, and end-to-end test patterns — and never-scanned vendored/build trees (the stack's single exclusion list; the exact classification is owned by the stack's checker) are never scanned; 0 and 1px are allowed; token definitions are not flagged; widths, heights, and font sizes are out of scope.

doesNotFire: The repository has no design root.

profileRequirements.meaning: The layer(s) beneath the design root that define the token values; files there are out of scope (that layer defines the values rather than consuming them).
profileRequirements.bunValue: `tokens` or `foundations` (first directory beneath the design root; other layers: `primitives`, `components`, `templates`)

profileRequirements.meaning: The notations in which this stack's UI files express the style declarations that are judged, including where a bare number counts as a length and how markup embedded in source literals is judged.
profileRequirements.bunValue: CSS declarations; JSX style objects (a bare number for the judged properties counts as a length, subject to the same > 1px threshold); in .ts/.mts files, inline style="…" attributes and <style> text in HTML authored in string, template, and tagged-template literals — only literal text is judged (code, comments, and regex literals are never read as declarations; a value spanning a ${…} interpolation is judged on its literal chunks alone)

profileRequirements.meaning: How a UI file references a foundations-defined token value instead of hardcoding it, and what defining such a token looks like (definitions are judged as definitions, never flagged).
profileRequirements.bunValue: referenced as `var(--…)`: a spacing, radius, or motion value defined once in foundations and referenced as `var(--…)`; a custom property definition such as `--space-3: 12px` defines a token wherever it lives and is not flagged

neutralityNotes: CSS property names (margin, gap, border-radius, transition…), px/ms units, and style-object/inline-style concepts are treated as the stack-neutral vocabulary of web UI styling, shared by every web stack; only the concrete notations (JSX style objects, HTML in .ts/.mts string/template/tagged-template literals) and the token-reference syntax (var(--…)) are stack-specific, and they are carried by the proposed profile keys idiom.responsive#style_notations and idiom.design_system#token_reference. The design root and its layers (design/design_system/design-system; tokens|foundations, primitives, components, templates) have no vocabulary key and are proposed as roots.design_system and layout.locations#design_token_layer. The core's test-file exclusion is the union of suffix.unit_test, suffix.acceptance_test, and suffix.e2e_test (each key keeps its own role: unit-test, acceptance-test, and e2e-test patterns); ATDD-Bun names all test kinds alike (*.test.*, *.spec.*), so under the Bun profile the union reproduces bun.json's single test-file exclusion exactly, while stacks with distinct patterns keep each kind excluded. The closed activation-fact vocabulary has no repository-structure or design-layer fact type, so the design-root prerequisite (facts[0]) and the layer exclusion (facts[2]) are encoded under the closest available type, 'role'. 'During GREEN' and the acceptance vocabulary are ATDD method terms, kept as neutral. Per notProfileKeys, this rule's detector/validator ids and its detector's current file-kind coverage (.tsx, .jsx, .html, .css, .ts, .mts) remain bunOnly, and severity 2 / strict disposition live in core:verification.
